 Divine generals
 Add TT as Preferred Source 
 Performers march in a parade of seven local Jiajiang troupes during the opening ceremony and street procession of the Jiajiang Art Festival in Chiayi City yesterday. The event included rituals to ward off bad luck and offer blessings, along with performances, highlighting Jiajiang culture as an important part of Taiwan’s cultural heritage, event organizers said.

 INDUSTRY RECOVERY: 
 Taisugar’s increase of live pigs is expected to stabilize domestic prices, which have seen a sharp increase due to tariffs and farming costs Taiwan Sugar Corp (Taisugar), a major pig farming operator in Taiwan, yesterday said that its pig count would recover to 200,000 as farm renovation completes next year, which is expected to help stabilize domestic pork prices. 
Taiwan’s wholesale pork price remained high at about NT$100 per kilogram since the end of May ahead of the Dragon Boat Festival this year, data from the National Animal Industry Foundation showed. 
The domestic supply of live pigs has been affected by several factors.

 Alice Huang (黃樂), the alleged Chinese spy involved in an extramarital affair with Nvidia Corp CEO Jensen Huang (黃仁勳), would not be able to return to Taiwan, as her entry permit has been revoked, Minister of the Interior Liu Shyh-fang (劉世芳) said today.
Speaking at a meeting of the Internal Administration Committee at the Legislative Yuan, Liu confirmed that Alice Huang had previously visited Taiwan, but is currently abroad.
The National Immigration Agency (NIA) is cooperating with national security units in its investigation, Liu said.

 ‘TOTALLY WRONG’: 
 Wavel Ramkalawan reiterated his opposition to his nation’s revocation of Lai’s overflight permit in April, while lauding bilateral commercial ties Former Seychelles president Wavel Ramkalawan on Thursday said that his government’s last-minute revocation of overflight permission in April for President William Lai’s (賴清德) chartered aircraft en route to Eswatini was wrong and should never happen again. 
“This [the decision] was totally wrong. And this is why I stood up, and the leader of the opposition also stood up to condemn that decision. And I hope this doesn’t happen again,” Ramkalawan said in an interview in Taipei.
